title.vi: Bài học phỏng vấn thực tập sinh máy song ngữ tách chủ đề

publication.scope_vi: Bộ học liệu thực tập sinh máy gồm ba mức trợ giúp tiếng Anh cho từng câu; không hạ yêu cầu an toàn hoặc thay thế huấn luyện thực hành được duyệt.

integration_guide_vi: Mỗi lesson là một câu hỏi độc lập và đúng ba key_points bắt buộc. Hiển thị các key_points thành ba gạch đầu dòng Anh–Việt.
Mã con giữ mã cha, ví dụ A052-STCW. Word và JSON dùng cùng mã bài và cùng nội dung từng gạch đầu dòng.
Bốn công ước trong A052 được tách riêng; sáu phụ lục MARPOL trong A051 cũng là sáu bài riêng. Bản này không thêm ngân hàng câu hỏi cho mọi công ước khác.
courses chỉ tham chiếu lesson_ids; phần chung không sao chép giữa ba khóa.
migration_from_v1 ánh xạ đủ 63 bài cũ sang bài mới. Giữ lịch sử cũ; không tự chuyển trạng thái đã đạt sang tất cả bài con.
legacy_source_lessons và provenance.original_parent_followups chỉ dùng biên tập tra cứu, không tự hiển thị thành bài đang học hoặc câu hỏi phụ của mọi bài con.
shared_vocabulary_parent_id trỏ đến shared_vocabulary.parent_id cho nhóm bài tách; không hiểu danh sách vocabulary rỗng là không có từ vựng.
model_answer ngắn chỉ là một cách diễn đạt; học viên cần bao phủ đủ ba ý khi đánh giá toàn câu, không cần giống nguyên văn mẫu.
Các asset âm thanh đang not_generated và uri=null. Chưa có tệp audio; cần tạo và duyệt trước bật nút nghe.
Giữ tiến độ học viên ở kho riêng theo learner_id + lesson_id + lesson_version. Các bài mới cần đánh giá lại.
Chỉ xuất bản sau duyệt chuyên môn và ngôn ngữ. Đây là học liệu phỏng vấn, không phải quy trình vận hành độc lập.
Phiên bản 3 thêm question.variants cho 44 câu nền tảng được biên tập lựa chọn. Mỗi câu có đúng ba mẫu tiếng Anh kèm nghĩa tiếng Việt trong dữ liệu; không phải thống kê tần suất phỏng vấn.
Word trình bày ba mẫu thành ba dòng tiếng Anh dưới câu hỏi gốc song ngữ. Cả ba mẫu dùng cùng ba ý bắt buộc, đáp án và tiêu chí của bài.
Cho học viên chọn cách hỏi qua variant_selection. Khi luyện nghe có thể chọn ngẫu nhiên một variant; lưu prompt_variant_id trong lần làm để biết học viên đã nghe mẫu nào.
Không xem ba mẫu là ba bài khác nhau; giữ cùng lesson_id khi lưu tiến độ. Câu canonical vẫn là câu chuẩn gốc.
variants rỗng nghĩa là bài chỉ dùng câu hỏi chuẩn; không tự tạo cách hỏi khác nếu chưa được duyệt.
Âm thanh cho từng mẫu đã có bản ghi assets nhưng uri=null: cần tạo và duyệt trước khi luyện nghe. Không suy ra học viên đã luyện một mẫu chỉ vì đã mở bài.
migration_from_v2 mô tả thay đổi cách hỏi; giữ lịch sử phiên bản 2. Không tạo ba bản sao tiến độ cho ba mẫu. Chính sách ôn với mẫu mới do giáo viên chọn.
Phiên bản 4 bổ sung hợp đồng tài khoản mua khóa, hồ sơ tên tuổi và mẫu trả lời cá nhân. Các thay đổi này là dữ liệu thiết kế; chưa triển khai đăng nhập, thanh toán hoặc máy chủ.
Tên và tuổi là bắt buộc lúc bắt đầu học. Trường học, tình trạng tốt nghiệp và kinh nghiệm được hỏi thêm khi mở bài có chỗ cần điền, không chặn các bài không dùng thông tin đó.
A001 dùng mẫu cá nhân hóa chứa tên tuổi và nhánh đang học/đã tốt nghiệp, đã thực hành/chưa thực hành. A010 và A017 dùng thông tin thực tế tương ứng.
Đọc personalized_answer_templates.languages, nối literal với profile_field và chọn nhánh choice theo hồ sơ. Không thực thi văn bản học viên nhập như mã hoặc chỉ dẫn AI.
Không tự điền trường học hoặc chứng chỉ từ tên và tuổi. Thiếu dữ liệu phải xin học viên khai thêm; vẫn cho xem đáp án tham khảo chung nhưng chưa đánh dấu câu cá nhân đã hoàn tất.
Không ghi câu đã điền vào model_answer chung. Nếu lưu hoặc tạo giọng đọc cá nhân phải gắn với tài khoản và phiên bản hồ sơ.
Nếu học viên đổi tài khoản, không dùng lại câu trả lời hoặc audio cache của người trước. Tài khoản được xác định từ phiên đăng nhập, không từ họ tên.
Tuổi do học viên nhập và xác nhận; không tự cộng tuổi theo năm vì không có ngày sinh. Nếu quá 365 ngày cần xác nhận lại trước khi đưa tuổi vào câu.
Âm thanh cũ của đáp án chung không được gắn nhãn là giọng đọc cá nhân. Tạo audio cá nhân là bước riêng, chưa được thực hiện trong gói dữ liệu này.
Phiên bản 5: mọi model_answer của câu chính phải hiển thị; không dùng chỉ dẫn ghép ý thay cho đáp án.
Mỗi follow_up_questions có model_answer riêng. model_answer_ref trỏ tới id đáp án câu phụ đó, không dùng đáp án cha làm đáp án hoàn chỉnh.
experience_example_only=true yêu cầu nhắc học viên thay bằng trải nghiệm thật; không tự lưu câu minh họa thành hồ sơ cá nhân.
Âm thanh đáp án cũ phải đánh dấu stale hoặc tạo lại nếu lời đáp án đã sửa; không tiếp tục phát tệp có lời không khớp.
Dữ liệu hồ sơ và mẫu cá nhân hóa phiên bản 4 được giữ; source_reference_answer được đồng bộ theo đáp án mới.

Phiên bản 6 có learning_material cho đủ 94 bài; mỗi bài có ba mức trợ giúp, 3–7 câu hỏi nhỏ có đáp án, ba cụm từ, ba bài nhớ cụm và một bài kiểm tra hiểu nghĩa có lời giải. Có 343 câu nhỏ trong toàn bộ ngân hàng.
Chọn mức theo learning_support_policy. Mức 1 không phải chức danh thấp hơn hoặc được phép giảm an toàn; chỉ tăng trợ giúp ngôn ngữ.
Hiển thị micro theo thứ tự một phần một lần ở Mức 1; không bung toàn bộ đáp án và bài tập cùng lúc. Cho lặp lại phần nhỏ rồi chuyển bước.
Các bài tập nhớ và chọn câu chỉ là luyện tập; không dùng làm bằng chứng đã đạt phần nói hoặc đầy đủ chuyên môn.
Mức 2/3 cùng dùng đáp án chính hoàn chỉnh trong model_answer. Câu nhỏ chỉ giúp tiếp cận khái niệm, không thay đáp án đầy đủ.
Mỗi câu phụ vẫn giữ model_answer riêng; ba mức không tạo ba bản sao bài học hoặc tiến độ mastery.
Đổi mức không xóa lịch sử nhưng phải lưu hỗ trợ đã dùng. Một câu trả lời có gợi ý không thành không trợ giúp chỉ vì chuyển sang Mức 3.
Các câu nói nhỏ có audio_scripts chờ tạo; không gắn nhãn đã có giọng đọc.

text.en: I want to become a competent engineer officer because I enjoy technical responsibility. First I must complete my approved training, assessed sea service and the applicable certification requirements. My next target is to complete this cadetship successfully; later dates depend on my progress and my training provider's approved route.
text.vi: Tôi muốn làm sĩ quan máy có năng lực vì thích trách nhiệm kỹ thuật. Trước hết tôi phải hoàn thành huấn luyện được duyệt thời gian đi biển được đánh giá và yêu cầu chứng nhận áp dụng. Mốc tiếp theo là hoàn thành tốt đợt thực tập; các mốc sau phụ thuộc tiến độ và lộ trình được cơ sở đào tạo duyệt.

text.en: A marine diesel engine converts fuel energy into mechanical power through compression ignition. For example, in a direct-drive installation the main engine turns the shaft and propeller. Other vessels may use gearing or electric propulsion, so I confirm the actual arrangement before describing it.

text.en: Engine heat passes into coolant and through heat exchangers to the final cooling medium, often seawater. The system includes circulation pumps, coolers and temperature-control arrangements as fitted. Correct temperatures protect components and maintain suitable operating conditions; both overheating and excessive cooling can cause problems.

Nhiệt độ đúng bảo vệ chi tiết và duy trì điều kiện làm việc phù hợp; quá nóng hoặc làm mát quá mức đều có thể gây vấn đề.

text.en: The authorised person identifies and isolates all relevant energy sources, applies the required locks and tags and verifies safe conditions. This includes stored pressure and possible movement, not only electrical power. I confirm permission with the person in charge before assisting and never remove another person's protection on my own.
text.vi: Người có thẩm quyền nhận diện cô lập các nguồn năng lượng liên quan khóa treo thẻ theo yêu cầu và kiểm chứng an toàn. Việc này gồm áp tích trữ và chuyển động không chỉ điện. Tôi xác nhận cho phép với phụ trách trước hỗ trợ và không tự tháo bảo vệ của người khác.

question.vi: Cô lập là gì?

short_answer.en: It separates equipment from its energy sources.
short_answer.vi: Cô lập tách thiết bị khỏi nguồn năng lượng.

short_answer.en: It helps prevent unauthorised re-energisation.

question.vi: Năng lượng tích trữ là gì?

question.vi: LOTO nghĩa là gì?

short_answer.en: LOTO means lockout and tagout of energy sources.

question.vi: Ai kiểm chứng cô lập an toàn?

short_answer.en: An authorised person verifies safe energy conditions.
short_answer.vi: Người có thẩm quyền kiểm chứng trạng thái năng lượng an toàn.

question.vi: Nguy cơ tích trữ nào có thể còn?

short_answer.en: Stored pressure and possible movement must also be controlled.

text.en: I confirm the permit, risk assessment, isolation, ventilation, tested atmosphere, attendant, communications and rescue arrangements. IMO recommendations specify normal oxygen of 20.9%; oxygen alone is not enough because toxic or flammable gases may still be present. The responsible person verifies results from suitable calibrated instruments against the applicable procedure before authorising entry.
text.vi: Tôi xác nhận giấy phép đánh giá rủi ro cô lập thông gió khí đã đo người trực ngoài liên lạc và bố trí cứu nạn. Khuyến nghị IMO nêu oxy bình thường 20,9%; riêng oxy chưa đủ vì có thể còn khí độc hoặc cháy. Người phụ trách kiểm chứng số đo từ thiết bị hiệu chuẩn phù hợp theo quy trình áp dụng trước cho phép vào.

text.en: A high-pressure fluid jet can penetrate the skin and cause a serious injury. Tightening or disturbing a pressurised fitting can release more fluid or cause movement. I keep clear, report it and wait for verified isolation and pressure release; any suspected injection injury needs urgent medical help.

text.en: I separate waste into the categories and containers specified in the Garbage Management Plan, including plastics, paper, rags, glass, wood and food waste as applicable. Plastics are retained for authorised disposal, not discharged at sea. Grinding food waste does not by itself authorise discharge; I follow the relevant location, treatment and disposal conditions.
text.vi: Tôi phân loại rác theo nhóm và thùng trong Kế hoạch quản lý rác gồm nhựa giấy giẻ thủy tinh gỗ và thức ăn khi áp dụng. Nhựa giữ để thải đúng nơi không xả biển. Nghiền thức ăn không tự cho phép xả; tôi theo điều kiện vị trí xử lý và thải liên quan.

prompt.en: Why must you check the garbage category, treatment, vessel location and applicable conditions rather than simply remembering 3 or 12 nautical miles?

text.en: Different waste categories have different restrictions, and some must not be discharged at all. Treatment, special-area or other local conditions and the vessel's location can change what is permitted. A remembered distance alone cannot establish that a particular discharge is lawful.

assets.text: Please introduce yourself and describe your university education in marine engineering in English.
My name is [name]. I study marine engineering at [university]. My relevant training includes [actual workshop or onboard experience].
Why did you choose marine engineering, and why do you want to work at sea?

I chose marine engineering because I enjoy machinery and practical problem-solving. Working at sea lets me develop these skills in an international team. I understand that sea life requires discipline, teamwork and time away from family.
Why should the company recruit you as an Engine Cadet?

I am willing to learn, follow instructions and work safely with others. In a workshop task, I checked the instructions and asked the instructor before using unfamiliar equipment. I would bring the same careful approach to your cadet programme.
What is your main strength as an Engine Cadet?
My main strength is carefulness. For example, during workshop practice I checked a tool's condition and confirmed the task before starting. This helps me avoid mistakes and support the team safely.
What is one area you need to improve?
I need to improve my spoken technical English. I practise answering one engineering question aloud each day and record myself. I compare new recordings with earlier ones to check my progress.
What does marine engineering cover?
It covers propulsion and auxiliary machinery. It includes electrical, control and refrigeration systems. It includes safe operation, maintenance and pollution prevention.
How would you assess your marine engineering course?

My course gave me a foundation in diesel engines, auxiliary machinery and safety. Workshop and simulator exercises helped me connect theory with practice. I still need supervised onboard experience to understand real systems and improve my practical skills.
Which subject did you enjoy most and why?

My favourite subject was marine diesel engines. I enjoyed learning how fuel energy becomes mechanical power and studying the engine cycle. This knowledge helps me understand propulsion machinery and the readings monitored on watch.
What are your career goals after your cadetship?

My next goal is to complete my approved cadet training and work towards qualification as an engineer officer. I need assessed TRB tasks, the required sea service and the applicable examinations. I will agree realistic target dates with my training provider and review them against my actual progress.
How long do you intend to stay with the company?

I hope to build a long-term career with the company. I value structured training, a safe working environment and opportunities to progress. I intend to keep developing my skills and discuss any circumstances affecting my plans honestly.
What is a seafarer?
A seafarer works on board a ship. Each crew member has assigned duties. Safe shipboard work requires discipline and teamwork.
What are the advantages of a seagoing career?
It provides practical maritime experience. It offers opportunities to develop technical skills. It provides experience working in an international team.
What are the challenges of a seagoing career?
Long periods away from family require preparation. Shipboard routines require discipline and adaptation. Work demands must be managed through safe practices and fatigue reporting.
How would you handle pressure, difficulties or unfamiliar work during your cadetship?

I stay calm and ask my supervisor to explain work I do not understand. For example, when a workshop task was unfamiliar, I asked for a demonstration and learned it step by step. If fatigue affects safety, I report it and request suitable rest instead of continuing unsafely.
Why is teamwork important on board?
Clear communication helps coordinate work safely. Repeating back instructions reduces misunderstanding. Each person supports the team within their competence.
How can a cadet demonstrate leadership and support others?

I can set an example by following safe practices and communicating respectfully. For example, during a group workshop task I repeated the instructions and checked that everyone understood their part. I support colleagues within my competence and refer decisions beyond my authority to the supervisor.
What documents and certificates have you prepared for the cadet programme?
I have prepared [actual documents and certificates]. I check their validity and the company's requirements, and identify anything still pending.
What are the duties, responsibilities and limits of an Engine Cadet's role?
I learn systems, assist with maintenance and join supervised watches. I follow the assigned engineer and do not operate machinery or keep a watch independently.
What specific outcomes do you want to achieve during this cadetship?

I want to understand the main systems, improve safe practical skills and communicate clearly. I will complete suitable TRB tasks with proper assessment. I will agree achievable tasks and review dates with my training officer.
When participating in a watch with an engineer officer, what should a cadet observe, record and report?

I observe assigned pressures, temperatures, levels, leaks, noise and vibration and record the actual readings. I report abnormalities promptly to the duty engineer. At handover I confirm ongoing work, machinery status and the instructions for my training duties.
What would you do if an alarm occurred during your training watch?
I identify the alarm and inform the duty engineer immediately. I observe safely and assist as instructed; acknowledging an alarm does not resolve its cause.
What would you do if you did not understand an order or were assigned a task you did not know how to perform?

I ask the person giving the order to clarify it and repeat it back in my own words. For an unfamiliar task I request an explanation or demonstration. I do not begin until I understand the job and the safe method.
If you made a mistake on board, how would you report it and learn from it?

I stop if the situation is unsafe, report exactly what happened and follow corrective instructions. I do not hide the error or attempt an unauthorised repair. Afterwards I review the cause with my supervisor and apply the agreed steps to prevent recurrence.
What maintenance have you participated in during workshop practice, simulation or onboard training? Describe the work you personally performed.

During [actual training], I assisted with [task] under supervision. I followed the safety instructions, reported the result to my supervisor and learned [specific lesson]. I distinguish work I personally assisted with from work I only observed.
Why is housekeeping important in the engine room, and how do you maintain it?
Good housekeeping reduces slips, fires and obstructed access. I clean after work, store tools correctly and report leaks.
How do you use your Training Record Book to plan and monitor onboard training?

I check that my TRB matches the approved training programme. I agree suitable tasks with my training officer and review progress regularly. I record gaps and agree the next training opportunities rather than marking unfinished tasks as complete.
How do you record a practical task in your TRB and request assessment and sign-off?
I record the date, equipment, actual work and outcome, distinguishing observation from supervised performance. I request assessment by an authorised assessor.
What would you do if you could not complete a TRB task because the equipment was not fitted or no practical opportunity arose?
I report the gap to my training officer and training provider and agree an approved alternative. I never claim an unperformed task.
What is a marine diesel engine, and what is the function of the main engine?

A marine diesel engine converts fuel energy into mechanical power through compression ignition. For example, in a direct-drive installation the main engine turns the shaft and propeller. Other vessels may use gearing or electric propulsion, so I confirm the actual arrangement before describing it.
Explain the two-stroke diesel engine cycle.
One cycle uses two piston strokes and one crankshaft revolution. Compression and combustion expansion produce mechanical work. Exhaust and scavenging exchange gases according to the engine design.
Explain the four-stroke diesel engine cycle.
The strokes are intake, compression, power and exhaust. One cycle requires two crankshaft revolutions. Valve timing controls gas exchange according to the design.
Compare two-stroke and four-stroke marine diesel engines.

A two-stroke completes a cycle in one revolution; a four-stroke in two. Their gas-exchange arrangements differ with design. Suitability and efficiency depend on the engine and service, not the cycle alone.
Identify the main engine components and explain their functions.
The piston receives gas force, the connecting rod transmits it and the crankshaft produces torque. The liner, cylinder head and valve gear support sealing and gas exchange.
What are the functions of piston rings?
Rings seal combustion gases and transfer heat to the liner. Oil-control rings, where fitted, regulate oil on the cylinder wall.
What is a turbocharger, and how does turbocharging work?

Exhaust gas drives the turbocharger turbine, which turns an air compressor. The compressor supplies pressurised air for combustion and, where applicable, scavenging. A naturally aspirated engine has no exhaust-driven turbocharger and takes in air without that boost.
What are the basic differences between a diesel engine and a gas-fuelled engine?

Diesel engines normally use compression ignition of injected liquid fuel. A gas-fuelled engine may use spark ignition or pilot fuel, so I first identify the design before comparing fuel supply and combustion. Gas-fuel systems need the specific leak-detection, ventilation and protective arrangements required by that installation.
Identify the main engine room machinery and equipment by their English names.

Main engine-room equipment includes the main engine for propulsion, generators for electricity, boilers for steam and pumps for fluid transfer. Compressors supply air, separators clean oil, and the OWS treats oily bilge water; a freshwater generator produces fresh water where fitted. I identify their actual positions and distinguish fitted equipment from equipment I have only studied.
What is the function of an air compressor on board?

An air compressor supplies compressed air for starting, control or service duties. For example, a starting-air compressor charges the starting-air receivers. I identify which system the actual compressor serves and use only the specified pressure and operating instructions.
What is a purifier used for, and how does it differ from a clarifier?

Centrifugal separation removes contaminants according to density differences. A conventional purifier separates oil, water and solids, while a clarifier mainly removes solids from oil. They support fuel or lubricating-oil treatment, with the actual arrangement depending on the separator design.
What is a marine boiler used for?

A marine boiler produces steam for services such as fuel heating, domestic heating or cargo heating where fitted. Important readings include steam pressure and water level, with other checks specified for the actual boiler. As a cadet I learn these checks and the steam consumers under supervision.
What is an emergency generator, and what is its role when the main electrical supply is lost?

The emergency generator supplies designated emergency consumers when the main electrical supply fails. I assist with assigned inspections or tests under the responsible engineer's supervision. I do not independently switch or test emergency electrical equipment.
What is the purpose of the cooling water system?

Cooling water removes heat from machinery and transfers it through heat exchangers to the final cooling medium. Pumps circulate the coolant through the relevant circuits. Maintaining the specified temperature prevents overheating and avoids problems caused by unsuitable operating temperatures.
What are the functions of lubricating oil in an engine?

Lubricating oil reduces friction and wear and removes heat from working surfaces. It also carries contaminants to filters or separators. In a typical circuit, a pump circulates oil through the cooler, filters and lubricated parts before it returns to the sump.
What is bilge water, and what is the function of a bilge pump?

Bilge water collects in low spaces and may contain oil or other contaminants. A bilge pump transfers it to the designated collection or treatment system; transfer is not permission to discharge overboard. I report suspected contamination and follow the authorised handling route.
What is a pump?
A pump adds energy to move fluid. It creates flow against the connected system's resistance. Its required flow and head depend on the service.
How are pumps classified by operating principle?
Centrifugal pumps transfer energy through a rotating impeller. Positive displacement pumps trap and displace volumes of fluid. Operating principle and service name are different classifications.
Give examples of shipboard pump applications.

Cooling-water pumps circulate cooling water, fuel-transfer pumps move fuel between designated tanks, and bilge pumps transfer bilge water to the assigned system. The fluid and duty determine the suitable pump type. I use the actual system diagram to identify the pump and its role.
What is refrigeration?
Refrigeration removes heat from a space or product. The heat is rejected to another medium. Shipboard uses include food storage and cargo cooling where fitted.
Explain the basic vapour-compression refrigeration cycle.

Refrigerant flows through compressor, condenser, expansion device and evaporator. The evaporator absorbs heat; the condenser rejects heat. The compressor and expansion device separate high and low pressure sides.
What is the difference between direct current and alternating current?
DC flows in one direction; AC reverses direction periodically. Batteries provide DC, while ship generators commonly provide AC; converters can change the supply form.
What is the difference between series and parallel circuits?
Series components carry the same current; parallel branches share the same voltage. An open circuit interrupts its current path; the effect depends on the actual circuit.
Which hand tools have you used and for what purposes?

In workshop practice, I used spanners for nuts and bolts and screwdrivers for matching screw heads. I selected the correct type and size and checked the tool's condition. I followed the instructor's method and did not use damaged tools.
Which measuring instruments have you used?

In workshop practice, I used a vernier calliper to measure external and internal dimensions and depth. I checked its condition and zero, selected a suitable range and read the scale carefully. I repeated the measurement where necessary to check the result.
What workshop-machine experience do you have?

During workshop training, I used a drilling machine under supervision and observed lathe work. The drilling machine makes holes; the lathe machines rotating workpieces. I checked the required guards and PPE and used machines only after training and permission.
What should you check before using a portable electric tool?

I check the tool, cable, plug, switch, guards and the required insulation or earthing. I confirm suitable PPE, the work environment and operating instructions. I report defects and do not use damaged equipment.
What is welding?

Welding joins materials using heat, pressure or both, depending on the process. Fusion welding melts the parent material. For example, shielded metal arc welding uses an electric arc and a flux-coated electrode to form the joint.
What is brazing?
Brazing melts a filler metal without melting the parent material. The filler liquidus temperature is above 450 degrees Celsius. Joint preparation and filler compatibility affect the result.
What is soldering?
Soldering melts a filler without melting the parent material. Its filler liquidus temperature does not exceed 450 degrees Celsius. The selected solder and method must suit the joint and service.
What must be confirmed before assisting with hot work on board?

Before assisting, I confirm the hot-work permit and person in charge. I check that the required isolation, atmosphere testing and combustible controls have been arranged. I confirm the fire watch and stop if the authorised conditions change.
What does occupational safety mean to you, and how do you maintain safe working practices?

I identify hazards, understand the task and follow the SMS and supervisor's instructions. I report unsafe conditions and stop if safety is uncertain. If the risk or method is unclear, I ask for clarification before starting.
How do you select and use PPE in the engine room?
I select suitable helmet, coveralls, safety shoes and task-specific hand, eye and hearing protection. I check condition and remember PPE does not remove the hazard.
What is LOTO, and why is it required before maintenance?

LOTO means isolating, locking and tagging relevant energy sources before maintenance. An authorised person verifies that safe energy conditions have been achieved. Stored pressure, electrical energy and possible movement must also be controlled as applicable before I assist.
What conditions must be confirmed before entering an enclosed space?

Entry needs authorisation, risk assessment, isolation, ventilation, verified atmosphere tests, an attendant, communication and rescue readiness. Normal oxygen is 20.9%; oxygen alone does not prove safety. I raise the alarm and never attempt an unprotected rescue.
What would you do on discovering a fire in the engine room?
I raise the alarm, report the location and follow my muster duties. I attempt first response only if trained, safe and with a clear escape route; otherwise I withdraw.
What are the elements of the fire triangle, and how do they relate to extinguishing a fire?

The fire triangle consists of heat, fuel and oxygen. Cooling removes heat, smothering limits oxygen and isolation removes the fuel supply. I select the method and agent for the actual material and hazards, such as live electricity.
How do you select equipment for an ordinary combustible fire?
Identify ordinary combustibles such as wood or paper. Use a labelled agent suitable for that material, commonly water where safe. Check for electrical and other hazards and keep an escape route.
How do you select equipment for a flammable-liquid fire?
Identify the liquid and check the extinguisher label. Select a compatible agent such as suitable foam or dry powder. Do not use a solid water jet that can spread burning liquid.
How do you select equipment for a fire involving live electrical equipment?

Report the fire and arrange electrical isolation through authorised personnel. Use an extinguisher labelled suitable for live electrical equipment. Account for CO2 exposure or other agent hazards and maintain escape.
How do you select equipment for a metal fire?
Identify the burning metal from a safe position. Use a specialist agent specifically suitable for that metal. Do not assume water, foam or general-purpose powder is suitable.
If you discover an oil leak, how would you report it and assist with the response?

I keep clear, report the leak's location and assist with containment as instructed. I never search for a pressure leak by hand or tighten a pressurised connection. I report any suspected fluid-injection injury immediately and seek urgent medical assistance.
What does MARPOL Annex I cover?
It addresses prevention of pollution by oil. Engine-room examples include oily bilge water and sludge handling. Follow applicable treatment, discharge and record requirements under supervision.
What does MARPOL Annex II cover?

It controls pollution by noxious liquid substances carried in bulk. It concerns relevant cargo residues and tank-washing arrangements. Handling and disposal must follow cargo-specific procedures and applicable requirements.
What does MARPOL Annex III cover?

It prevents pollution by harmful substances carried in packaged form. Requirements include relevant packing, marking and documentation controls. Report damaged packages or leaks and follow assigned emergency instructions.
What does MARPOL Annex IV cover?
It addresses pollution by sewage from ships. Approved treatment or holding arrangements apply as required. Discharge depends on applicable conditions, not permission to pump alone.
What does MARPOL Annex V cover?
It addresses pollution by garbage from ships. Segregate and handle waste according to the Garbage Management Plan. Plastics must not be discharged at sea; check conditions for other categories.
What does MARPOL Annex VI cover?
It addresses air pollution from ships. It includes relevant SOx, NOx and energy-efficiency or carbon-intensity requirements. Confirm the requirements applicable to the ship, equipment, area and date.
What is STCW and how does it relate to an Engine Cadet?

STCW sets standards for training, certification and watchkeeping for seafarers. Cadet training follows an approved programme with assessed practical competence. Cadet training does not itself authorise independent engineering watchkeeping.
What is SOLAS and why is it important to engine-room personnel?

SOLAS is the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea. It sets ship safety requirements including relevant machinery, electrical and fire-safety provisions. A cadet learns emergency arrangements and follows assigned muster duties.
What is MARPOL and what is its purpose?

MARPOL is the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships. Its six technical annexes address different pollution categories. Engine-room personnel follow applicable handling, discharge and record requirements.
What is MLC 2006 and how does it protect seafarers?

MLC 2006 is the ILO Maritime Labour Convention. It addresses working and living conditions such as agreements, rest, accommodation and care. Seafarers should understand applicable rights and report concerns through established procedures.
How do you segregate, collect and manage garbage on board?
I follow the Garbage Management Plan, segregate waste and use marked containers. Plastics must not be discharged at sea; other disposal depends on category, location and applicable conditions.
What is the purpose of an oily water separator?

An OWS treats oily machinery-space bilge water. Oil-content monitoring and alarm arrangements depend on the approved installation. A cadet observes or assists only as assigned and never bypasses controls.
What must be checked before discharging treated machinery-space bilge water?

A reading not exceeding 15 ppm alone is not sufficient permission to discharge. The responsible officer confirms all applicable area, operational and equipment conditions. Report doubts and wait for confirmation; never dilute or bypass to evade controls.
What is the Oil Record Book and what machinery-space operations are recorded?

It records oil-related operations specified by the applicable requirements. Part I includes relevant machinery-space operations such as bunkering, sludge and bilge handling. Entries need accurate dates, quantities and operation details as required.
What is a cadet's role in preparing Oil Record Book information?

I collect and provide accurate data under supervision. The responsible authorised personnel make and sign required entries. I report discrepancies and never invent, conceal or alter records improperly.
What are ECAs and SECAs?

An ECA is a designated emission control area under MARPOL Annex VI. SECA refers to sulphur emission controls; other ECA controls may concern NOx. The applicable pollutant, area, equipment and effective date must be confirmed.
How does a cadet prepare for entering an applicable emission control area?

I confirm the applicable requirements and the engineer's instructions before entry. I assist with authorised fuel changeover or approved operating arrangements only as assigned. I monitor and record the specified parameters and report abnormalities.
When learning about tanker cargo support systems, how do you prepare for and record familiarisation visits and practical training in cargo areas?

I agree the visit with my training officer and the deck team, review cargo hazards and confirm access controls. I check communications and the limits of my assigned duties. Afterwards I record only what I observed or performed under supervision.
When assisting with maintenance or hot work on a tanker, how do you coordinate with your training officer and the deck department?
I confirm permission, cargo-operation restrictions, isolation, gas testing and fire-watch arrangements with the responsible officers. I start only when authorised and stop if conditions change.
On a bulk carrier, what safety conditions must you clarify before learning to inspect bilges or assisting with maintenance inside a cargo hold?
I confirm cargo hazards, fumigation status and enclosed-space controls with the responsible officer. An open hatch does not prove safe entry; I enter only after authorisation and verified checks.
When learning about lifting appliance maintenance on a heavy lift ship, how do you gather information and participate in the work?
I check equipment identification, safe working load, inspection records and the maintenance plan. I confirm isolation and supervision, and report defects to the responsible engineer or officer.
When training in Ro-Ro ramp hydraulic system maintenance, how do you confirm safety and follow the work?

I confirm isolation, pressure release and approved mechanical securing against ramp movement. I keep clear of oil jets, report leaks and never check them by hand. I do not tighten or dismantle a connection that may still be pressurised.
When assigned to learn about container refrigeration, how do you relate the refrigeration cycle to observations of an actual reefer unit?

I identify the compressor, condenser, expansion device and evaporator on the reefer. I record the container number, displayed readings and alarms and discuss abnormalities with my training officer. I do not change cargo settings or intervene without assigned authority and instructions.
When learning about reefer power supplies on a container ship, how do you distinguish observation from work requiring isolation and an authorised person?

I visually check accessible cables and connectors as instructed and report damage without touching exposed live parts. Switching, connection work, opening panels and electrical tests require authorised personnel. I assist only within my training after the appropriate isolation is confirmed.

I am currently studying marine engineering at [university]. My practical training includes [actual workshop or onboard experience]. I distinguish observation from work I personally performed under supervision.

I enjoy understanding machinery and solving practical problems. Going to sea gives me a chance to develop these skills and work with an international crew. I am prepared to learn, communicate clearly and follow the discipline required on board.

I want to become a competent engineer officer because I enjoy technical responsibility. First I must complete my approved training, assessed sea service and the applicable certification requirements. My next target is to complete this cadetship successfully; later dates depend on my progress and my training provider's approved route.

I hope to stay long term if I can keep learning and progressing in a safe working environment. I expect clear training objectives and constructive feedback. I will discuss any personal circumstances affecting my availability honestly rather than make promises I cannot keep.

During an unfamiliar workshop task, I paused and asked the instructor to demonstrate the method. I repeated the steps and practised them one at a time under supervision. This taught me to ask early and confirm understanding instead of guessing.

I tell the duty engineer or training officer that fatigue is affecting my ability to work safely. I explain the task and my condition and request suitable rest or reassignment. I do not hide the problem or continue a safety-sensitive task without guidance.

I present my actual academic records, safety-training certificates and joining documents required by the company and authorities. I check their validity and list any item still being processed separately. I do not claim to hold a document that has not been issued.

I learn systems, assist with maintenance and housekeeping and join watches under supervision. The Chief Engineer leads the engine department; I follow the assigned reporting line through the responsible engineers and training officer. I am a trainee, not the officer in charge of the watch.

I want to understand system flow paths, use basic tools safely and communicate accurate observations. I will practise professional conduct and record suitable assessed tasks in my TRB. I review these goals with my training officer so I am ready for the next approved training stage.

On assigned rounds I check temperatures, pressures and levels and look for leaks, unusual vibration or noise. I record actual readings without inventing values. I report abnormal conditions promptly to the duty engineer and assist as instructed.

I need machinery status, ongoing work, outstanding alarms and any special instructions for my duties. I pass on my readings and observations at handover. Starting or stopping machinery, operating valves, changing settings and responding to faults require the instructions or supervision appropriate to my training role.

I identify the alarm and report its location and observed symptoms to the duty engineer immediately. I monitor safely and assist as instructed. Silencing the buzzer or acknowledging the alarm only changes its indication; the underlying fault may remain and worsen.

I would say, Could you explain that again, please? I then repeat the instruction in my own words to confirm it. If I still do not know the method, I ask for a demonstration and wait until the safe procedure is clear.

I report what I did, the equipment involved and what I observed, without hiding details. I follow the responsible engineer's corrective instructions and discuss how to prevent recurrence. Concealment delays control of the risk, and an unauthorised repair can make the situation worse.

In a supervised workshop exercise, I helped clean a filter after the instructor confirmed safe isolation. I used the instructed tools, kept the parts clean and had the completed work checked by the supervisor. I learned to confirm isolation and report the result rather than assume the equipment was ready.

I keep floors and access routes clean and unobstructed, store tools correctly and remove waste to designated containers. I report leaks and clean spills using the approved method. This reduces slips, fire hazards and delays during emergencies.

I confirm the TRB edition and task requirements with my training provider and training officer. We agree tasks suited to the actual equipment and available opportunities. We review completed and outstanding items regularly and adjust the plan without falsifying completion.

I record the date, equipment, my actual role, work performed and outcome, with suitable evidence. I state clearly whether I observed or performed work under supervision. Only an assessor qualified and authorised under my approved programme should assess and sign the task.

I inform my training officer of the missing equipment or opportunity and contact the training provider through the agreed procedure. We seek an approved alternative or later opportunity and leave the task outstanding until requirements are met. Recording work I did not perform would misrepresent my competence.

Fuel burns in the cylinder after compression ignition and pushes the piston. The connecting rod and crankshaft convert this force into torque. In a direct-drive example the crankshaft drives the shaft and propeller; geared or diesel-electric installations have different transmission paths.

The piston receives combustion force, the connecting rod transmits it and the crankshaft converts it into torque. The liner and cylinder head form the cylinder and combustion space. A camshaft or another fitted control arrangement operates the relevant valves or injection equipment according to the engine design.

Compression rings limit combustion-gas leakage and transfer heat from the piston to the liner. Oil-control rings, where fitted, regulate oil on the cylinder wall. I identify the actual ring arrangement because crosshead and trunk-piston engines do not necessarily use identical ring functions.

The exhaust turbine drives a compressor that supplies pressurised air. A naturally aspirated engine has no such exhaust-driven air boost. In a turbocharged two-stroke, the air system supports scavenging and combustion, with auxiliary air arrangements depending on the design.

I first clarify the fuel and ignition design. A diesel normally injects liquid fuel for compression ignition; a gas engine may use spark ignition or pilot fuel, and a dual-fuel engine can use different approved modes. Fuel preparation, mixture formation and safety arrangements must be compared for that particular design.

The main engine provides propulsion, generating sets supply electricity and boilers supply steam. Compressors supply air, pumps move fluids, separators clean oil, an OWS treats oily bilge water and a freshwater generator produces fresh water where fitted. I use the actual layout and system diagrams to locate them rather than assume every vessel has the same arrangement.

Starting-air compressors charge receivers used for engine starting. Other compressors or air systems may supply control instruments and service tools at their specified pressures. I identify which compressor supplies each system from the actual diagram and instructions.

A rotating separator uses density differences to separate the phases. In a conventional purifier, solids collect at the bowl periphery and water is separated from the oil through the designed outlets. This removes water and solids from fuel or lubricating oil; a clarifier mainly separates solids from oil, depending on its design.

Steam may heat fuel, serve domestic systems or heat cargo where the ship is equipped for it. I learn to monitor the actual boiler's water level, steam pressure and the other checks in its instructions. I identify the consumers fitted on that vessel and observe or assist only under supervision.

The emergency generator supplies the emergency switchboard and designated services such as emergency lighting and other required consumers. I confirm the actual distribution from the ship's diagrams. During inspection or testing I perform only assigned checks under supervision and report defects.

Engine heat passes into coolant and through heat exchangers to the final cooling medium, often seawater. The system includes circulation pumps, coolers and temperature-control arrangements as fitted. Correct temperatures protect components and maintain suitable operating conditions; both overheating and excessive cooling can cause problems.

Oil forms a film that reduces contact and wear, removes heat and carries contaminants away. In a typical circuit a pump supplies oil through cooling and filtration to the working parts, and the oil returns to the sump or drain tank. I identify the actual circuit and monitoring points before describing it as my vessel's system.

Bilge water can come from drains, leaks or cleaning and may contain oil or other contaminants. It collects at designated bilge wells and is transferred to the assigned holding or treatment arrangement. Treatment and overboard discharge are separate operations requiring the applicable controls and authorisation.

Batteries supply DC, while ship generators commonly supply AC to motors and other consumers. A device receiving AC may rectify it to DC internally; an inverter can convert DC to AC. I distinguish the incoming supply from the voltage and current form inside the equipment.

In series, components carry the same current and the supply voltage is shared between them. In parallel, branches have the same supply voltage and carry their own currents. An open component breaks its series path, while other parallel branches can remain supplied; a lighting string must be analysed from its actual wiring.

I inspect the cable, plug, switch and guards and check the insulation or earthing required for that tool class. I confirm suitable PPE, a safe work area and the operating instructions. A damaged or unsuitable tool is reported and not used.

Before starting I identify hazards, understand the task and confirm the procedure with the person in charge. I check the required controls and communicate any concerns. If conditions are unsafe or unclear, I stop and ask for guidance.

I use the required helmet, coveralls and safety footwear, plus suitable hand, eye and hearing protection. Additional protection depends on the job and risk assessment. I check condition and fit and remember PPE supports, but does not replace, control of the hazard.

The authorised person identifies and isolates all relevant energy sources, applies the required locks and tags and verifies safe conditions. This includes stored pressure and possible movement, not only electrical power. I confirm permission with the person in charge before assisting and never remove another person's protection on my own.

I confirm the permit, risk assessment, isolation, ventilation, tested atmosphere, attendant, communications and rescue arrangements. IMO recommendations specify normal oxygen of 20.9%; oxygen alone is not enough because toxic or flammable gases may still be present. The responsible person verifies results from suitable calibrated instruments against the applicable procedure before authorising entry.

I raise the alarm immediately, give the exact location and keep others from entering impulsively. I follow my assigned duties and assist the trained rescue team as instructed. I do not enter without the planned rescue controls, equipment and authorisation.

I raise the alarm, report the location and follow my muster duties, including isolation assistance only as instructed. First response is attempted only when I am trained, the agent is suitable, conditions are safe and escape is clear. I withdraw if smoke, heat or fire conditions exceed those limits.

For an ordinary solid fire, suitable water cooling may remove heat when electrical and other hazards allow it. For a flammable-liquid fire, a compatible foam may separate the fuel surface from air, while fuel isolation removes the supply. I check the actual agent label and avoid methods that spread the fire.

From a safe position I identify the leak location and notify the duty engineer. I help protect the area and contain the spill with the approved materials as instructed. I report the condition and do not approach a suspected pressure jet.

A high-pressure fluid jet can penetrate the skin and cause a serious injury. Tightening or disturbing a pressurised fitting can release more fluid or cause movement. I keep clear, report it and wait for verified isolation and pressure release; any suspected injection injury needs urgent medical help.

I separate waste into the categories and containers specified in the Garbage Management Plan, including plastics, paper, rags, glass, wood and food waste as applicable. Plastics are retained for authorised disposal, not discharged at sea. Grinding food waste does not by itself authorise discharge; I follow the relevant location, treatment and disposal conditions.

Different waste categories have different restrictions, and some must not be discharged at all. Treatment, special-area or other local conditions and the vessel's location can change what is permitted. A remembered distance alone cannot establish that a particular discharge is lawful.

I confirm cargo hazards such as flammability, toxicity and oxygen deficiency with the responsible officers. I check required atmosphere tests, entry permission, ventilation, communications and the attendant or rescue arrangements applicable to the space. I enter or assist only within my assigned training duties and authorisation.

The responsible engineering and deck officers confirm whether the work is compatible with current cargo operations and terminal restrictions. Before I assist, the permitted area, isolation, atmosphere checks, permit and fire watch must be confirmed. If cargo operations or permit conditions change, I stop and report for reassessment.

Some cargoes consume oxygen or release toxic gases, and fumigation can leave dangerous residues or gas. Opening the hatch does not prove that all parts of the hold are safe. I wait for the responsible officer's verified entry controls, including cargo and fumigation status, ventilation and the required atmosphere tests.

I check the equipment identity against its records, rated load and current inspection status. I confirm isolation and supervision with the person in charge before joining maintenance. I report any defect to the responsible engineer or officer before the equipment is returned to service.

The responsible person isolates the system, safely releases stored pressure and confirms approved mechanical securing against movement. I keep clear of a leaking jet and report it immediately. I never search by hand or tighten or dismantle a connection before safe conditions are verified.

I record the container identification, displayed readings, alarm codes and the time, without changing the settings. I give these facts to my training officer and discuss what they may indicate. Any intervention must follow the assigned authority and the cargo or equipment instructions.

I visually inspect accessible cable insulation, plugs and connectors as instructed and report damage without touching exposed live parts. A cadet must not independently connect or disconnect supplies, switch equipment, open electrical panels or perform electrical tests. These tasks need authorised personnel and the appropriate safe isolation.

Source documents and original question cross references

All 4 sources were reviewed. S04 has no text layer; all 3 pages were read directly from the scanned images, comprising 13 Safety questions and 22 Technical Engine questions. English and Vietnamese versions of the same question in S01 were counted once.
Consolidation principles

Questions with the same assessment objective are combined into one main question. The Safety section of S04 almost entirely repeats that of S02. Questions on two-stroke/four-stroke engines, refrigeration/the refrigeration cycle, series/parallel circuits and DC/AC are grouped by topic, retaining requirements for sketches, comparisons, examples and applications in the follow-up questions.

Points clarified during compilation

Engine Cadet with a TRB: this bank is intended for university students training to become engineer officers. A019 to A021 were added for this purpose and were not present in the sources. The TRB format, assessment process and signatories must follow the approved programme and instructions of the university, company and competent authority.

Watchkeeping responsibilities: S03 uses "watchkeeper", while S04 gives only a brief description of the rank structure. A011/A013/A014 clarify the cadet's supervised training role; they do not authorise independent watchkeeping or handling every alarm as the officer in charge.

Engine cycles: S04 contains inconsistent statements about strokes and crankshaft revolutions. A023 retains the explanation and comparison requirements without reproducing inconsistent answers. Claims that two-stroke engines are always simpler, cheaper or twice as powerful, or that four-stroke engines are always more durable or cleaner, are not presented as universal conclusions.

Gas engines and electrical circuits: the diesel/gas comparison in S04 is incomplete. A027 requires clarification of the engine type before comparison. A039 retains the lighting string as an example to analyse from its circuit, without assuming all such strings are series-connected. A038 distinguishes the incoming supply from power after conversion within the equipment.

MARPOL and oil content: the S01 question on oil content before discharge does not identify the waste stream. A054 specifies oily machinery space bilge water and does not treat 15 ppm as either a sufficient discharge condition or a universal limit for every waste stream. A046 combines oxygen questions with the full entry and rescue requirements, rather than treating a single oxygen reading as sufficient.

Vessel classification: most original questions concern common engine room knowledge. Parts B, C and D contain 7 extension scenarios with core question codes and references. A TRB practical task must not be recorded as completed on equipment not fitted on board.

text.vi: Cần cho phép, đánh giá rủi ro, cô lập, thông gió, kiểm tra khí được xác nhận, người trực ngoài, liên lạc và sẵn sàng cứu nạn. Oxy bình thường là 20,9%; chỉ số oxy riêng không chứng minh an toàn. Tôi báo động, không tự vào cứu khi thiếu bảo vệ.

text.en: I visually check accessible cables and connectors as instructed and report damage. Switching, connection work, opening panels and electrical testing require authorised personnel and appropriate isolation.
text.vi: Tôi quan sát dây và đầu nối tiếp cận được theo hướng dẫn, báo hư hỏng. Đóng cắt, đấu nối, mở tủ và thử điện cần người có thẩm quyền cùng cô lập phù hợp.

instructions.en: Replace bracketed details with truthful personal information before recording.
instructions.vi: Thay nội dung trong ngoặc bằng thông tin cá nhân trung thực trước ghi âm.

interviewer_intent.en: Explain and apply the following ideas within the Engine Cadet role: Visually inspect accessible cables and connectors as instructed; Refer switching, connection, panel access and testing to authorised personnel
interviewer_intent.vi: Thể hiện hiểu biết và khả năng áp dụng trong vai trò thực tập sinh máy: Quan sát dây đầu nối tiếp cận được theo hướng dẫn; Để người có thẩm quyền đóng cắt đấu nối mở tủ và thử điện

follow_up_guidance.vi: Kiểm tra, báo tình trạng dây và đầu nối theo hướng dẫn; thực tập sinh không được tự làm những thao tác điện nào?

response_hint.en: Answer directly, add relevant technical detail, and state your actual experience or limits when relevant.
response_hint.vi: Trả lời thẳng câu hỏi, bổ sung ý kỹ thuật phù hợp và nêu kinh nghiệm thật hoặc giới hạn nhiệm vụ khi liên quan.

prompt.en: How should you check and report cable and connector condition as instructed? Which electrical operations must a cadet not undertake independently?
prompt.vi: Bạn kiểm tra và báo tình trạng dây, đầu nối theo hướng dẫn thế nào? Thao tác điện nào thực tập sinh không được tự làm?

follow_up_questions.assessment_note_vi: Dùng các ý liên quan đến câu hỏi phụ; không bắt học viên nhắc toàn bộ đáp án chính. Giảng viên cần duyệt chi tiết trước chấm tự động.

description.en: Independently connect, switch, open or test electrical equipment.
description.vi: Tự đấu nối đóng cắt mở hoặc thử thiết bị điện khi chưa được phép.

assessment.scope_vi: Đáp án mẫu ngắn là điểm xuất phát. Phần hỏi thêm có thể cần giải thích hoặc ví dụ ngoài đáp án mẫu; phải đánh giá theo phạm vi câu đang hỏi.
